government.note: Federal presidential republic under the Constitution as amended in 1994. The President is head of state and of government, elected with the Vice President for four years with one consecutive re-election (1994 amendment). Presidential elections use 'ballotage': a candidate wins in the first round with more than 45% of the vote, or with 40% and a lead of more than 10 percentage points; otherwise the top two meet in a run-off. When both the presidency and the vice presidency are vacant, the Provisional President of the Senate, then the President of the Chamber of Deputies, exercise the executive until Congress elects a president (December 2001). The National Congress has a Chamber of Deputies (257, half renewed every two years) and a Senate (72, one third renewed every two years; indirectly elected by provincial legislatures until the first direct election in 2001).

system.note: Proportional representation in 24 multi-member constituencies (the 23 provinces and the City of Buenos Aires), D'Hondt method with a 3% threshold. Half of the chamber (127 or 130 seats) is renewed every two years for four-year terms. Since 2011 candidacies are settled in open, simultaneous and mandatory primaries (PASO).

system.note: Three senators per province and the City of Buenos Aires: the most-voted list wins two seats and the runner-up one. One third renewed every two years for six-year terms. Senators were chosen by the provincial legislatures until the first direct election in 2001, when all 72 seats were renewed.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the October 1999 Chamber of Deputies vote: Alianza 45.89% (split as an estimate about 55/45 between the UCR, counted as social liberal, and FREPASO, social democrat), Justicialist Party 38.63% (big tent: Peronism spans left and right; under Menem it governed with market reforms), Action for the Republic 8.12% plus the Union of the Democratic Centre (liberal conservative), provincial parties such as the Neuquén People's Movement, Republican Force and the Democratic Party of Mendoza (regionalist), and the Trotskyist and communist left (United Left, Workers' Party; mapped to marxist_leninist). In the 1999 presidential election De la Rúa won 48.37%, Duhalde 38.28% and Cavallo 10.22%.

claims.note: Argentina claims the Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas), South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, administered by the United Kingdom; the claim is written into the transitional provisions of the Constitution as amended in 1994 (Wikipedia: Falkland Islands sovereignty dispute).
